enrichment.jsDocDescription: A heading component for an asset that displays the asset name, its current sync/design status (e.g. 'Up to date', 'Sync with dev', 'Redesign needed', 'Not used'), and a descriptive text about usage context.
enrichment.notes: The root is best represented as a section since it groups a heading, a status badge, and a description. The status badge (e3/e4) is conditionally shown depending on the variant. Consider using an appropriate heading level (h2 or h3) for the asset name based on page hierarchy.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A subheading component for assets that displays a subtitle label and an optional description. Supports variant states indicating asset sync status (Up to date, Sync with dev, Redesign needed, Not used) and a toggleable description text.
enrichment.notes: The 'Rectangle 1' shape likely serves as a status indicator or divider visible in most variants. The description text is conditionally rendered based on the 'Show description' boolean prop. Consider using aria-describedby to associate the description with the subtitle when visible.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A primary neutral button component with support for default, disabled, hover, and loading states across multiple sizes and light/dark modes.
enrichment.notes: Use aria-disabled=true when State is Disabled instead of the HTML disabled attribute if you need to keep the element focusable. When State is Loading, consider adding aria-busy=true and an aria-label that communicates the loading state to assistive technologies.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A destructive primary button used to trigger irreversible or high-risk actions such as deletions. Supports Default, Disabled, Hover, and Loading states in Regular, Large, and Small sizes, with Light and Dark mode variants.
enrichment.notes: Use aria-disabled='true' when State is 'Disabled' rather than the HTML disabled attribute to maintain focusability if needed. When State is 'Loading', consider adding aria-busy='true' and updating aria-label to indicate the in-progress state (e.g., 'Deleting...'). The destructive nature should be communicated clearly via label text or aria-label.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A subtle variant of the primary button component, supporting default, disabled, hover, and loading states across multiple sizes and light/dark modes.
enrichment.notes: Use aria-disabled=true when State is Disabled rather than the HTML disabled attribute if you need to keep the element focusable. When State is Loading, consider adding aria-busy=true and an aria-label that communicates the loading state to assistive technologies.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A primary action button with an optional icon and neutral styling. Supports multiple states (default, disabled, hover, loading) and sizes (small, regular, large) in both light and dark modes.
enrichment.notes: Use aria-disabled=true and avoid setting the native disabled attribute when you need the button to remain focusable in the disabled state. The loading variant should update aria-label to indicate loading status, e.g. 'Loading…'. The icon (Edit instance) is decorative and its inner SVG should carry aria-hidden=true.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A destructive primary button with an icon, used to trigger delete or irreversible actions. Supports multiple states (Default, Disabled, Hover, Loading) and sizes (Small, Regular, Large) in both Light and Dark modes.
enrichment.notes: Use aria-disabled='true' and avoid removing the element from the DOM when in Disabled state. When in Loading state, consider adding aria-busy='true' to indicate an ongoing process. The destructive variant should be visually distinct (e.g., red/danger color) to communicate the irreversible nature of the action.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A subtle primary button component that supports an optional leading icon and a loading state indicator. Renders in multiple sizes (Small, Regular, Large) and color modes (Light, Dark), with states for Default, Hover, Disabled, and Loading.
enrichment.notes: Use aria-disabled='true' instead of the HTML disabled attribute when the Disabled variant is active, to preserve focusability for screen readers. When in the Loading state, consider adding aria-busy='true' and visually hiding the loading indicator label. The icon (e1) is decorative and should have aria-hidden='true' on the underlying SVG.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: An icon-only primary button in neutral style. Triggers an action without a text label, relying solely on an icon for visual communication. Supports Default, Hover, and Disabled states across Regular, Large, and Small sizes in both Light and Dark modes.
enrichment.notes: Since this button contains only an icon and no visible text label, an aria-label must always be provided to describe the button's action for screen readers. The aria-disabled attribute should be set to true when the Disabled variant is used.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: An icon-only primary button with destructive styling, used to trigger irreversible or delete actions. Supports Default, Hover, and Disabled states across Regular, Large, and Small sizes in Light and Dark modes.
enrichment.notes: Since this button contains only an icon (no visible text label), an aria-label is required for accessibility. The destructive variant typically uses red/danger color tokens. Ensure the icon conveys the destructive intent clearly. When in Disabled state, set aria-disabled to true and prevent click handlers.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: An icon-only primary button in its subtle variant. Displays a single icon without a background by default, used for compact or low-emphasis actions. Supports multiple states (default, hover, disabled) and sizes (tiny, small, regular, large) in both light and dark modes.
enrichment.notes: Since this button contains only an icon and no visible text, an aria-label must always be provided to describe the action it performs. The 'Default (no BG)' state indicates a ghost/subtle style with no background fill. Ensure the icon inside uses aria-hidden='true' to prevent redundant screen reader announcements.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A secondary neutral button component with support for default, disabled, hover, and loading states across multiple sizes and light/dark modes.
enrichment.notes: Use aria-disabled=true when State is Disabled instead of the HTML disabled attribute if you need to keep the element focusable. The loading variant should include an aria-label or aria-busy attribute to communicate loading state to assistive technologies. Map the Size and Mode variants via CSS classes rather than separate components.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A secondary destructive action button used to indicate potentially harmful or irreversible actions. Supports multiple states (Default, Disabled, Hover, Loading) and sizes (Small, Regular, Large) in both Light and Dark modes.
enrichment.notes: Use aria-disabled='true' when State is 'Disabled' rather than the HTML disabled attribute to maintain focusability if needed. When State is 'Loading', consider adding aria-busy='true' and updating aria-label to indicate the loading state. The destructive nature should be communicated clearly in the button label or via aria-describedby pointing to a warning message.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: An icon-only secondary button with a neutral style. Triggers an action without a text label, relying solely on an icon for visual communication. Supports Default, Hover, and Disabled states across Regular, Large, and Small sizes in both Light and Dark modes.
enrichment.notes: Since this button contains only an icon and no visible text label, an aria-label must always be provided to describe the button's action for screen readers. The aria-disabled attribute should be set to true when the Disabled state variant is used.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A tertiary neutral button component used for low-emphasis actions. Supports multiple sizes (Small, Regular, Large), light/dark modes, optional icon, and interactive states including hover and disabled.
A tertiary destructive button used to trigger irreversible or high-risk actions. Supports icon display, multiple sizes, light/dark modes, and interactive states including hover and disabled.
enrichment.notes: Use aria-disabled=true when the State variant is 'Disabled' to preserve focusability while communicating the disabled state. The destructive nature should be conveyed through visible label text (e.g., 'Delete', 'Remove'). No additional aria-label is needed if the button text is descriptive.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A subtle tertiary button component used for low-emphasis actions. Supports multiple sizes (Small, Regular, Large), light/dark modes, optional icon, and interactive states including hover and disabled.
enrichment.notes: Use aria-disabled='true' when the Disabled variant is active. The 'Has icon' property controls visibility of a leading icon (e1). Prefer this button for tertiary actions that require minimal visual weight.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: An icon-only tertiary button with neutral styling. Displays a single icon without a text label, used for compact or supplementary actions. Supports Default, Hover, and Disabled states in both Light and Dark modes.
enrichment.notes: Since this button contains only an icon (no visible text label), an aria-label is essential for accessibility. The aria-label should describe the action performed, derived from the icon used (e.g., 'Add'). When State is 'Disabled', set aria-disabled to true and prevent click interactions.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: An icon-only tertiary button with a subtle visual style. Supports default, hover, and disabled states in both light and dark modes. Use when a low-emphasis action needs to be represented by an icon alone.

enrichment.notes: Since this button contains only an icon (no visible text), an aria-label is required to convey the button's purpose to assistive technologies. The 'Subtle' variant implies minimal visual styling. Ensure the icon instance (Add) is aria-hidden to avoid redundant announcements.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A link-styled button component that navigates to a URL or triggers an action, available in multiple sizes and visual modes with support for default, hover, and disabled states.
enrichment.notes: Despite being named 'Link button', if it triggers navigation use the <a> tag with an href attribute. If it triggers an action without navigation, consider using a <button> tag instead. The 'aria-disabled' attribute should be set to true when the State variant is 'Disabled'. Ensure sufficient color contrast for both Light and Dark modes.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: An icon-only button component that triggers an action. Supports default and hover interaction states, low and high importance variants, and light and dark display modes.
enrichment.notes: Since this is an icon-only button, an aria-label must always be provided to describe the button's action for screen readers. The tooltip (e2) appears conditionally in some variants and may serve as supplemental description; consider linking it via aria-describedby when visible.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: An icon-only primary toggle button with a subtle visual style. Supports default, disabled, hover, and selected states across multiple sizes and light/dark modes.
enrichment.notes: Since this is an icon-only button, an aria-label must be provided to describe the action or toggled state. Use aria-pressed instead of aria-expanded if this is a stateful toggle (pressed/unpressed). The 'Selected' variant state should map to aria-pressed='true'.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: An icon-only secondary toggle button with neutral styling. Supports multiple states (default, hover, active, disabled) and sizes (small, regular, large) in both light and dark modes.
enrichment.notes: Since this is icon-only, an aria-label must be provided to describe the button's action for screen readers. The 'Active' state may warrant aria-pressed='true' to convey toggle state. Consider using aria-pressed (boolean) to reflect the toggled state, though this attribute is not in the allowed schema set.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A compact micro-sized button component used to trigger actions. Supports default and hover interaction states.
A button that copies a URL to the clipboard. Displays the URL text alongside an icon button, with visual states for default, hover, and copied confirmation. Supports light and dark display modes.
enrichment.notes: The 'Copied' state should update aria-label to 'Link copied' or use aria-live to announce the clipboard action to screen readers. The URL text (e1) is decorative in context but may be useful as visible feedback.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A button that copies a URL to the clipboard. Displays the current URL with a copy icon, and transitions to a 'Copied' confirmation state (with a check icon) for 2 seconds before reverting. Supports a descriptive label beneath the URL.
enrichment.notes: The component has Default, Hover, Copied, and Disabled states. Use aria-disabled='true' on the Disabled variant. The 'Copied' state should ideally use aria-live or an aria-label update to announce the copy confirmation to screen readers. The optional Description text (e.g. 'Default UXfolio URL') can be linked via aria-describedby.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A Floating Action Button (FAB) in neutral style. Triggers a primary or contextual action and optionally displays a tooltip. Supports Default, Hover, and Selected states across Regular, Small, and Tiny sizes in Light and Dark modes.
enrichment.notes: FAB components should always have a descriptive aria-label since they typically contain only an icon. The tooltip (e2) is conditionally rendered and should be linked via aria-describedby when visible. Ensure the button's purpose is clearly communicated through aria-label in the absence of visible text.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A Floating Action Button (FAB) in a subtle style variant. Triggers a primary or contextual action, available in Regular, Small, and Tiny sizes with Light and Dark mode support.
enrichment.notes: The 'Subtle' variant implies a lower visual emphasis compared to a standard FAB. The optional tooltip (e2) should be associated via aria-describedby when visible. Use type='button' to prevent unintended form submission.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A Floating Action Button (FAB) variant for destructive actions (e.g., delete). Renders with a delete icon and optionally a tooltip. Available in Regular, Small, and Tiny sizes, with Light and Dark modes, and Default and Hover states.
enrichment.notes: This is a destructive FAB, typically used for irreversible actions like deletion. Ensure the aria-label clearly communicates the destructive nature of the action. The tooltip (e2) is conditionally rendered and should be associated via aria-describedby when visible.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A navigation button used in the editor navigation bar. Supports icon-only, label-only, or combined icon and label display modes, with selected, default, and hover states.
enrichment.notes: Use aria-pressed or aria-selected to indicate the selected state depending on context. If used within a nav element, consider wrapping the set of buttons in a <nav> with an appropriate aria-label.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A navigation button linking to the Account settings page. Supports Default, Hover, and Selected visual states to indicate the current page or interaction state.
enrichment.notes: Use aria-current='page' when the Selected state is active to indicate the current page to assistive technologies. The component likely belongs inside a nav element as part of a site navigation menu.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A navigation button that takes the user back to the previous page or step. Displays a left arrow icon alongside a 'Back' label.
A button component for adding a new page or social link. Renders with default and hover interaction states.
Displays a user's avatar image, typically used to represent a person or account visually. Supports default and hover interaction states.
enrichment.notes: Consider using an img tag if the avatar is purely an image element, or a button if it triggers navigation or actions on click. The hover state suggests possible interactivity. Ensure alt text or aria-label is provided for accessibility.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A toolbar button component with optional icon, label, and dropdown indicator. Supports multiple states (default, hover, selected, disabled) and can appear in text or icon-only mode with light or dark theme variants.
enrichment.notes: Use aria-expanded and aria-haspopup when Dropdown is True. Set aria-disabled instead of the HTML disabled attribute when you need to keep the element focusable. The 'Selected' state may warrant aria-pressed if used as a toggle button.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A toolbar button used to select or apply a color, with optional dropdown affordance. Supports default, hover, and selected states in both light and dark modes.
enrichment.notes: The 'Type' variant determines whether a chevron (up or down) is shown, indicating dropdown behavior. When Type is 'Dropdown', aria-haspopup and aria-expanded should be set appropriately. The 'Selected' state should reflect aria-pressed or a visual selected indicator.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A destructive toolbar button that triggers a delete or irreversible action. Supports Default, Hover, and Selected states in both Light and Dark modes.
enrichment.notes: This button represents a destructive action (e.g., delete). Ensure it is clearly labeled and consider adding a confirmation dialog before executing the action. The aria-label should reflect the specific destructive action it performs.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A toolbar button displaying a status indicator (e.g. 'Draft') with an optional icon. Supports default and hover states in light and dark modes.
A toggle switch component that represents a boolean on/off state. Renders as a checkbox input styled as a switch, supporting both light and dark visual modes.
enrichment.notes: Should use type='checkbox' with role='switch' for proper accessibility. The 'State' variant (True/False) maps to the checked/unchecked state. The 'Mode' variant (Light/Dark) is a visual-only concern and does not affect semantics. The Thumb element (e1) is a decorative shape used for the visual indicator of the switch position.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A radio button toggle component that allows users to select a single option from a group. Supports true/false (selected/unselected) states and light/dark display modes.
enrichment.notes: This component represents a single radio button input. The 'State' variant (True/False) maps to the checked/unchecked state of the input. Should be wrapped in a label element and grouped with other radio inputs using a fieldset and legend for accessibility. The ellipse shape (e1) is only visible in 2 of 4 variants, likely representing the inner dot indicator when the radio is selected.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A checkbox input component that toggles between checked (True) and unchecked (False) states, available in light and dark display modes.
enrichment.notes: The root should render as <input type='checkbox'>. The State variant ('True'/'False') maps to the checked/unchecked state. The Mode variant ('Light'/'Dark') controls visual theming and should be handled via CSS classes rather than ARIA attributes. Wrap with a <label> element if a visible text label is needed.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A small tab component that allows users to switch between different views or sections. Supports optional top or side icons, and renders in light or dark mode with default, hover, and active states.
enrichment.notes: Use within a tablist container (role='tablist'). Set aria-selected='true' on the active tab. The 'Active' state variant corresponds to the selected tab. The 'Highlight' shape (e5) likely serves as a visual indicator for the active state.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A large tab component that allows users to switch between different content panels or views. Supports optional top or side icons, and renders in light or dark mode with default, hover, and active states.
A single item within an option bar (segmented control), representing a selectable option that can display either text or an icon. Supports active/inactive and hover states.
enrichment.notes: This component behaves as a tab within a segmented control / option bar. Use aria-selected instead of aria-pressed, and wrap multiple items in a container with role='tablist'. The 'Active' variant property maps to aria-selected state.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A draggable slider thumb control that represents the current value position within a range input. Rendered as a styled thumb handle for a range slider.
enrichment.notes: This component represents the draggable handle of a range slider. It should be used in conjunction with a slider track and ideally implemented as an <input type='range'> or with appropriate ARIA role='slider' attributes including aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, and aria-valuenow.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A button component that allows users to add a color, with default and hover interaction states.

A labeled text field component that displays an input area with an associated label, current value, and optional helper text or status icons. Supports multiple states (Default, Active, Success, Filled, Hover, Error, Disabled) and light/dark modes.
enrichment.notes: The root element wraps a label, input value, and optional helper text/icons. Use a native <label> element (e2/e5) associated with the corresponding <input> via htmlFor/id. The helper text (e10) should be linked to the input via aria-describedby. Status icons (e7 Check, e8 Danger) should have appropriate aria-label or aria-hidden attributes depending on whether they convey meaning redundantly.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A search text field component with multiple states (Default, Active, Filled, Hover, Disabled, Error). Renders a styled search input with an associated label and optional error message.

A labeled dropdown list component that displays a subheader label above an input field with a value and a chevron icon indicating open/closed state. Supports default, hover, active, and disabled states in light and dark modes.
enrichment.notes: This is a dropdown/select-style component with a label (Subheader/Small), an input field showing the current value, and a chevron icon that toggles between up and down depending on open/closed state. The popover list appears only in active/open variants. Use aria-expanded to reflect open state and aria-controls to reference the popover list element.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A labelless dropdown trigger control that displays a current value and a chevron icon to indicate an expandable list. Supports default, hover, active, and disabled states in light and dark modes.
enrichment.notes: The component lacks a visible label, so an aria-label should be provided by the consuming context to describe the dropdown's purpose. The aria-expanded attribute should be toggled dynamically based on whether the popover list is open or closed.

It has multiple variants including Home, Page, Case study, Long case study, View portfolio, and View case study. The root nav tag reflects its navigational purpose, though a ul/li structure may be more appropriate if multiple items are rendered together in a list context.

enrichment.notes: Each Field row contains a checkbox (Toggle/Checkbox instance) and a text label. The root is best represented as a fieldset grouping related checkbox controls. Supports Light and Dark visual modes.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: An option chip component that represents a selectable filter or category option. Supports default, hover, and active interaction states.
enrichment.notes: Option chips are typically used for filtering or selecting from a set of options. Consider using aria-pressed if the chip toggles a selected state, or aria-selected if used within a listbox/tablist context. The embedded media (logo/icon) may need aria-hidden if decorative.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A font size picker control that allows users to select or input a font size value. Supports dropdown-only, text-and-dropdown, and text-only interaction modes with default and hover states.
enrichment.notes: The component has multiple type variants (Dropdown only, Text & dropdown, Text only), suggesting it may render as a combobox or spinner input in implementation. Consider using a native <input type='number'> or <select> depending on the active variant. The root div with role='group' wraps the label and control elements.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A font size picker control for a platform UI, supporting dropdown-only, text-and-dropdown, and text-only variants. Allows users to select or input a font size value.
A palette swatch selector component that displays a group of color swatches, allowing the user to select one. Supports multiple selection states and picker variants (Default, Editor).
enrichment.notes: The component contains multiple swatch instances acting as a radio-button-like selection group. Using fieldset semantically groups the related swatch controls. Each swatch (Only swatch instance) should internally render as a button or input[type=radio] with appropriate aria attributes.

A color selector component that allows users to choose between different color or gradient styles (Dark gradient, Solid, Light gradient). Renders a labeled section with color option buttons.
enrichment.notes: The component contains a subheader label and a horizontal row of color option instances. The variant type (Solid, Dark gradient, Light gradient) likely controls which color options are visible. Consider using a fieldset/legend pattern if the color options are radio-button-like choices, but since the root contains mixed content (header + controls), a div with role=group is appropriate.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: Vector artwork rendered from exported SVG assets.
A section option item displaying an icon alongside a label and bold statement text. Used as a selectable or informational row within a list of options, grouped under a section heading.
enrichment.notes: The component has Default and Hover states, suggesting it may be interactive (selectable). If used within a listbox or menu, ensure the parent has the appropriate role (e.g., listbox or menu) and this element carries role='option' or role='menuitem' accordingly. The bold statement text appears only in some variants, so handle its conditional rendering carefully.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A selectable option item representing a case study entry, featuring an icon, label, bold statement, and an optional checkbox toggle. Supports default and hover states, as well as active/inactive selection states.
enrichment.notes: The component behaves as a selectable option (with Active True/False and Default/Hover states), making it suitable as a button with aria-pressed or a checkbox-like control. The embedded Toggle/Checkbox instance suggests it may function as a multi-select option item. Consider using aria-pressed if used as a toggle button, or wrapping in a form context if used as a checkbox group item.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: An option box component that allows users to select a color option, either from a suggested palette or via a custom color picker. Supports default, hover, and active interaction states.
enrichment.notes: The component has two types: 'Suggested color' and 'Custom color', and three states: Default, Hover, and Active. The Micro button sub-element appears only in some variants (likely the Custom color type). Consider using aria-pressed if this acts as a toggle/selection control, or aria-selected if used within a listbox context.

The 'Color override' and 'Mode' variants are purely visual and require no additional ARIA attributes.

enrichment.notes: The root is a div acting as a styled text container. The 'Has toolbar' boolean toggles a toolbar module, and 'Reaching limit' toggles a character limit tooltip. Consider using a native textarea element if this is an editable field, or a div with role='textbox' and aria-multiline='true' if it is a rich text editor.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A text underlay component that provides a blurred background surface behind text content, optionally extended with a module extension variant.
enrichment.notes: The component appears to be a purely decorative blur/overlay element used as a background for text. It likely has no semantic meaning on its own and may warrant aria-hidden='true' in implementation. The single child element is a blur shape, suggesting this is a visual styling container.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A responsive image box component that renders an image container with configurable size variants, ranging from flexible/fluid sizing to fixed grid-based sizes (3–12 columns) or full width.
enrichment.notes: The root element is best represented as a div since it acts as a sized container for an image. Consider using a figure element if captions are needed, though it's not in the allowed set. The 'Full' and numeric size variants suggest a grid/column-based layout system. Ensure the inner image instance has appropriate alt text for accessibility.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A content block component that displays an image with an optional caption. Supports interactive states (Default, Hover, Active, Passive), light/dark modes, and editing controls including a toolbar, drag handle, and move left/right actions for repositioning within a layout.
enrichment.notes: The 'Active' state reveals resize anchors, a toolbar, drag handle, and move controls, suggesting this is an editable/CMS-style image block. The role='figure' is appropriate when the image and caption are grouped semantically. Consider aria-describedby pointing to the caption element for accessibility.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A tightly-cropped image box component that displays a fixed image with optional resize handles and container anchors. Supports Default, Hover, Active, and Active Free states in both Light and Dark modes.
enrichment.notes: The component appears to be an image container with interactive resize/anchor handles visible in certain states. The 'Tight' variant likely refers to reduced padding or a snug crop around the image. Since it wraps an image instance and includes resize anchors, it may be used in a canvas or layout editor context. Consider aria-label reflecting the image content when used in production.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A preview image box component that displays a fixed image in either light or dark mode, with default and active visual states. Typically used to represent selectable or highlighted image previews in a gallery or selection UI.
enrichment.notes: The component has Default and Active states suggesting it may be interactive (selectable). If used as a selectable item, consider wrapping in a button or adding tabindex and keyboard interaction. The 'Container' shape only appears in 2 of 4 variants, likely representing an active/selected overlay or border highlight.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A testimonial box component that displays a customer or user quote, typically including a review or endorsement. Supports multiple size variants for flexible layout integration.
enrichment.notes: Using <article> as it represents a self-contained piece of content (a testimonial/quote) that could stand independently. Size variants (Flexible, 4, 5, 6, 8) likely correspond to column-span or grid-width options. Consider adding a cite element inside for attribution if the design includes an author name.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A testimonial card component that displays a user quote, attribution text, and an optional avatar image. Supports light and dark modes, and multiple interaction states (Default, Hover, Passive, Active).
enrichment.notes: Use within a list of testimonials (ul) for semantic grouping. The 'Has image' boolean prop controls avatar visibility. Toolbar, Drag, and Resize container elements appear to be editor/design-tool UI overlays and should not be rendered in production HTML.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A column item card component that can display an optional image, optional added text, a primary text block, and an optional action button. Supports interactive states (Default, Hover, Passive, Active) and light/dark modes, with editor-mode controls for reordering and resizing.
enrichment.notes: The component appears to be a content card used within a column layout. The toolbar, resize anchors, drag handle, and move FABs are editor/authoring UI controls visible only in certain variants (likely edit mode). In production rendering, the article tag is appropriate for a self-contained content card. If items are rendered in a list context, consider wrapping multiple instances in a ul and using li semantics at the parent level.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: An embedded media box component that displays a flexible image with an optional caption, toolbar, resize handles, drag functionality, and navigation controls for repositioning the media within a layout.
enrichment.notes: The component supports multiple states (Default, Hover, Active, Passive, Empty) and light/dark modes. The resize anchors and drag handle suggest this is an editable/interactive media block in a rich content editor context. The Move left/right FAB buttons allow repositioning the block within a layout. Use a descriptive aria-label reflecting the media content when possible.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A form box component containing a group of user input fields and a submit button, with optional descriptive text, resize handles, toolbar, drag handle, and navigation controls for repositioning the form within a layout.
enrichment.notes: The root is a form since it contains multiple User input fields and a submit button. The 'Move left/right' and toolbar/drag instances suggest this form box can be repositioned in a canvas or module-based layout. The 'Has text' boolean likely toggles a description or helper text above the form. Use aria-label to give the form a meaningful accessible name in context.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: Represents a single step or item within a multi-step process or wizard flow, supporting previous/next connectors and various interaction states (Default, Hover, Active, Passive) in both light and dark modes.
enrichment.notes: This component is designed to be used inside a process/stepper list. The 'Has next' and 'Has previous' props control connector lines between steps. The 'State' variant (Active, Passive, etc.) should be reflected via aria-current='step' when active. Since li is not allowed as root htmlTag per schema, use div with role='listitem' and ensure it is wrapped in a ul/ol parent.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A logo box component that displays a flexible image/logo with optional move controls (left/right FAB buttons) and a toolbar. Supports hover, active, and default states in both light and dark modes.
enrichment.notes: The component includes directional move controls (FAB buttons) that are conditionally shown based on 'Move left' and 'Move right' boolean props. The toolbar and drag handle suggest this may be a repositionable widget within a layout editor or canvas. Consider adding aria-live or more specific roles if the logo position updates dynamically.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A case study card component displayed outside a module context, featuring a thumbnail image (optionally with a designer overlay and gradient), descriptive text, and an optional CTA button. Supports multiple layout orientations (Top, Bottom, Right, Left), light/dark modes, and interactive states including Default, Active, Hover, and Passive.
enrichment.notes: The component appears to be a card-style element showcasing a case study, with optional move/resize controls suggesting it may be used in an editable canvas or builder context. The 'Outside' naming likely refers to its placement relative to a module or container. Use a semantic <article> as each card is a self-contained piece of content. Ensure the thumbnail image has descriptive alt text and the CTA button has an accessible label.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A case study card component displayed within a layout, featuring a thumbnail image, text content, optional CTA button, and editor controls (move, resize, drag) for repositioning within a canvas. Supports light/dark modes and multiple layout types (Small, Center, Left, Right).
enrichment.notes: The 'Inside' suffix suggests this is the inner content of a case study card, possibly embedded in a larger carousel or grid. Editor-only controls (move, resize, drag anchors, toolbar) should be aria-hidden in production. The optional CTA and thumbnail designer image are conditionally rendered based on props.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A case study card component that displays a thumbnail image with optional designer mockup, overlay, title/description text, and interactive controls. Supports hover, active, and passive states with light/dark modes, and includes optional navigation (move left/right) and resize handles for editor/active contexts.
enrichment.notes: The component represents a self-contained case study preview card. In Default/Hover/Passive states it functions as a content card (article); in Active state it gains resize handles, a toolbar, and drag affordances suggesting an editor context. The 'Has CTA' prop controls visibility of a call-to-action button. Use aria-label to provide a meaningful case study title for screen readers.

enrichment.jsDocDescription: A case study thumbnail card component used in a portfolio or content grid. Supports light/dark modes, hover/active states, and optional designer image overlay. Includes controls for repositioning (move left/right) and resizing anchors, suggesting it is used within an editable or interactive layout builder context.
enrichment.notes: The 'Hidden' variant likely means the card is not visible in the published view but is present in the editor. The move and resize controls (FABs, anchors, drag handle, toolbar) are editor-only UI and should be aria-hidden in production. Consider wrapping editor controls with aria-hidden='true'.
